selection_rationale: One coherent combination: the pinned public OpenAPI spec, stripe-python 16.0.0 and stripe-node 23.0.0 all target Stripe API version 2026-09-30.endive (spec info.version, stripe/_api_version.py, src/apiVersion.ts). The consumer templates pin these SDK versions and send Stripe-Version 2026-09-30.endive. accept-a-payment pins the older API version 2023-10-16 and older SDKs, so it is used only as an integration-pattern reference, never as a contract snapshot to compare against.
evidence_boundaries: The OpenAPI spec is Stripe's published contract, not Stripe's server implementation.
The SDKs are outbound clients: their methods map to API operations but are not Stripe server handlers.
stripe-mock serves spec-driven, hardcoded responses (stateless; no response control); it is not Stripe production behavior.
accept-a-payment is an official sample application showing integration patterns; it is not a Stripe customer or Stripe source.
No source in this lock gives access to Stripe's production server implementation; provider source discovery for Stripe is reported as unavailable.

sources.role: evaluated, not used for the simulated change
sources.decision: Not used. Its README states responses are hardcoded and stateless, and specific responses cannot be requested; its embedded payment_intent fixture has amount 1099. It cannot return the old/proposed response pair, so the demo uses a focused local fixture server configured through the SDKs' supported base-URL options.

sources.version_mismatch: The sample pins Stripe API version 2023-10-16 (apiVersion in server.js; stripe.api_version in server.py) with stripe ^20.2.0 (Node) and stripe==14.2.0 (Python). The demo templates use 2026-09-30.endive with stripe-node 23.0.0 and stripe-python 16.0.0, so the sample is not compared against the pinned contract snapshot. Its Payment Element servers expose merchant routes (GET /, GET /config, GET /create-payment-intent, POST /webhook); /create-payment-intent calls PaymentIntent create, not retrieve. These are merchant routes, not Stripe API operations.
